**Tip (E049, 3df6233).** This is E036 plus a group-2 freeze (anneal 75→90%, frozen for the last 10%) plus +0.25 epoch, for 237 steps at batch 2000.
- Resolution: 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%. The whitening is detached from 20% and the stem frozen from 75%.
- Two builds of the same commit read 0.7535 at 5.198 s (E049) and 0.7552 at 5.206 s (E050). The tip's population mean is probably about 0.7535–0.754, slightly better than E036's (~0.7528).
- The cascade was close to free: E046 saved 0.265 s for about −0.05 pp, and the top-up cost 0.12 s.

**Noise.**
- The 3-seed mean of identical math moves about ±0.25 pp across rebuilds. A null change passes 0.753 about 50% of the time on this tip.
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp and the 20-seed SE about 0.07 pp. Time reproduces to about 1%.
- E050 did not show bit-identical pinning. Within-build cuDNN atomics are still my main suspect.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ steps × per-step cost.
- Per step: 32 px 0.032 s, 28 px 0.026 s, 24 px 0.021 s, 20 px 0.016 s.
- The stem freeze saves about 27% of a 32 px step. The group-2 freeze saves another ~0.010 s per step.
- Truncation is worth 1.5–2× its FLOP share because it also skips memory-bound BN/GELU backward, the optimizer and Lookahead traffic (H6.6; E046 beat me).
- Fused elementwise kernels are about 27% of a 32 px step. These are bytes-bound, so swapping the activation saves at most about 2%.
- The 31×31 stem tensor (conv1 output feeding the pool) is the biggest single memory-bound cost in unfrozen steps.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5. Stem freeze at 75%: about 2. Group-2 freeze at 90%: close to free (>3).
- Freeze at 60%: a cliff (~0.65). Width: about 0.7. Selection at 90–95%: about 2–2.5, ambiguous.
- Removing inductive bias (stride instead of pool, ReLU instead of GELU) is probably below 1 s/pp.

**Funders.** All 6 boosters tested read ≤0. My prior for a new one is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy is bought with steps, and frozen 32 px steps are the cheapest steps.

**Mechanisms**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum (E005, E025, E030).
2. The late 28/32 px phases and a stem that trains until about 70–75% carry accuracy (E018, E024, E037, E040, E041).
3. Early accuracy depends on step count and the LR schedule, not on pixels (E026, E033, E045).
4. Backward truncation with an annealed LR is the dominant cheap lever (E028, E036, E046, E049). Its dose is limited by the anneal window. For group 2, 85% is probably still gentle, with ~13 more frozen steps saving about 0.13 s.
5. Muon renormalizes filters every step, so filter wd has no effect.
6. Max-pool after conv1 is an accuracy-bearing prior. A stride-2 conv saves a lot of time (~8–10%) but probably costs 0.5–1 pp on CIFAR-100.

**Strategy.**
- Extend the group-2 freeze dose (I082) and fund it with frozen 32 px top-up steps.
- Stack math-identical systems trims.
- Selection is marginal.
- The PCIe judge adds about 5–10% to time, and its own rebuild adds accuracy risk, so keep about 0.2 pp of population margin.

**Unsure**
- The held-out delta of the group-2 freeze at 85%.
- Whether a stride-2 stem plus a large top-up beats the dial.

W3 (cost lens), after E050.

**Tip (E049, 3df6233).** This is E036 plus a group-2 freeze (anneal 75→90%, frozen for the last 10%) plus +0.25 epoch, for 237 steps at batch 2000.
- Resolution: 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%. The whitening is detached from 20% and the stem frozen from 75%.
- Two builds of the same commit read 0.7535 at 5.198 s (E049) and 0.7552 at 5.206 s (E050). The tip's population mean is probably about 0.7535–0.754, slightly better than E036's (~0.7528).
- The cascade was close to free: E046 saved 0.265 s for about −0.05 pp, and the top-up cost 0.12 s.

**Noise.**
- The 3-seed mean of identical math moves about ±0.25 pp across rebuilds. A null change passes 0.753 about 50% of the time on this tip.
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp and the 20-seed SE about 0.07 pp. Time reproduces to about 1%.
- E050 did not show bit-identical pinning. Within-build cuDNN atomics are still my main suspect.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ steps × per-step cost.
- Per step: 32 px 0.032 s, 28 px 0.026 s, 24 px 0.021 s, 20 px 0.016 s.
- The stem freeze saves about 27% of a 32 px step. The group-2 freeze saves another ~0.010 s per step.
- Truncation is worth 1.5–2× its FLOP share because it also skips memory-bound BN/GELU backward, the optimizer and Lookahead traffic (H6.6; E046 beat me).
- Fused elementwise kernels are about 27% of a 32 px step. These are bytes-bound, so swapping the activation saves at most about 2%.
- The 31×31 stem tensor (conv1 output feeding the pool) is the biggest single memory-bound cost in unfrozen steps.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5. Stem freeze at 75%: about 2. Group-2 freeze at 90%: close to free (>3).
- Freeze at 60%: a cliff (~0.65). Width: about 0.7. Selection at 90–95%: about 2–2.5, ambiguous.
- Removing inductive bias (stride instead of pool, ReLU instead of GELU) is probably below 1 s/pp.

**Funders.** All 6 boosters tested read ≤0. My prior for a new one is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy is bought with steps, and frozen 32 px steps are the cheapest steps.

**Mechanisms**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum (E005, E025, E030).
2. The late 28/32 px phases and a stem that trains until about 70–75% carry accuracy (E018, E024, E037, E040, E041).
3. Early accuracy depends on step count and the LR schedule, not on pixels (E026, E033, E045).
4. Backward truncation with an annealed LR is the dominant cheap lever (E028, E036, E046, E049). Its dose is limited by the anneal window. For group 2, 85% is probably still gentle, with ~13 more frozen steps saving about 0.13 s.
5. Muon renormalizes filters every step, so filter wd has no effect.
6. Max-pool after conv1 is an accuracy-bearing prior. A stride-2 conv saves a lot of time (~8–10%) but probably costs 0.5–1 pp on CIFAR-100.

**Strategy.**
- Extend the group-2 freeze dose (I082) and fund it with frozen 32 px top-up steps.
- Stack math-identical systems trims.
- Selection is marginal.
- The PCIe judge adds about 5–10% to time, and its own rebuild adds accuracy risk, so keep about 0.2 pp of population margin.

**Unsure**
- The held-out delta of the group-2 freeze at 85%.
- Whether a stride-2 stem plus a large top-up beats the dial.
- The source of within-build nondeterminism.

forecasts.reason: The fused kernels are bytes-bound, so ReLU saves only ~1.5% (below the 3% bar), and losing GELU's smoothness likely costs 0.2–0.3 pp on CIFAR-100.
Removing the 31×31 conv and pool saves ~8% of time, but dropping the max-pool prior costs ~0.8 pp, about 0.55 s/pp, which is worse than the dial.
A net 5-step cut saves ~0.1 s, and selection has been close to the dial's rate; the change is too small to resolve with 20 seeds.
~13 more frozen group-2 steps save ~0.13 s for perhaps −0.05 to −0.1 pp; the accuracy delta is likely inside the noise.

cruxes: What is the held-out accuracy cost per frozen group-2 step between 85% and 90%? If it is near zero, the cascade dose (and a frozen-step top-up) is the cheapest remaining lever.
Does a stride-2 stem (I080) lose more than 0.5 pp of the 20-seed mean? If it loses under 0.3 pp, its ~0.4 s saving funded by a top-up would beat every other lever.
Is the tip's population mean (E049/E050: 0.7535/0.7552) really about 0.754? That decides how much margin can be spent before the 0.753 gate and the PCIe judge's rebuild risk bite.
